cpu_zaya1_8b.notes: Real forward()+generate() loop via create_cpu_backend() (tests/test_backend.cpp), not a synthetic kernel microbenchmark -- genuine tokenizer round-trip and real weights on disk. Single-pass first-token latency was 4.37 tok/s; 2.5 tok/s is the steady-state 5-token benchmark average, used here as the representative figure.

npu_xrt_hw_validate.notes: Raw device-level validation, NOT a model-inference tok/s number: 51 TOPS INT8 GEMM, 50us avg latency, 74735-75404 op/s throughput via `xrt-smi validate`. Confirms the NPU hardware/driver/firmware stack is healthy on this box today. Also today: fixed a real buffer-overflow segfault in engine/fusion/zero_copy/test_pipeline_real (the GPU+NPU zero-copy fusion kernel test) -- it now runs its 28-layer synthetic pipeline to completion without crashing, exercising real NPU GEMM (XRT) + real GPU attention (HIP) kernels on hardware. That test's own wall-clock is NOT included here: its per-layer NPU/GPU overlap loop has a separate, pre-existing, unrelated bug (NPU FFN is only invoked once instead of per-layer) that would make a tok/s figure from it misleading. No end-to-end NPU model-decode tok/s was measured this pass -- the existing npu_v12 (69 tok/s) and npu_flm (57 tok/s) entries are carried forward unchanged and their measurement dates are untraced; don't assume they're current.
